written.title: Over 20 years later, GTA Vice City is still a role model for the open-world genre
written.description: What GamesRadar+, Kotaku and Push Square reported about Vice City on 29 October 2026, quoted in their own words with a link to each report.
written.body:
This page collects what named outlets published about Vice City, in their own words. This site wrote none of the sentences in quotation marks below. Each one links to the report it was taken from.

## GamesRadar+, 29 October 2026

[Over 20 years later, GTA Vice City is still a role model for the open-world genre](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/grand-theft-auto/over-20-years-later-gta-vice-city-is-still-a-role-model-for-the-open-world-genre/)

The outlet's own summary:

> Returning to the sunny streets of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City ahead of GTA 6's own homecoming

> Similarly, the Dodo can soar dozens of feet off the ground, but it quickly and inevitably reaches the limit of its engine power and slumps back down to earth.

> Every Friday GamesRadar+ Your weekly update on everything you could ever want to know about the games you already love, games we know you're going to love in the near future, and tales from the communities that surround them.

> It's up to you which businesses you want to buy and which of their accompanying mission chains you want to follow, but all of them are ultimately connected to Tommy Vercetti's core goal of constructing his criminal empire.

> There's no swimming, climbing walls or moving while crouching in Vice City, but there are celebrity voiceovers, a fully licensed soundtrack, and a recognisable representation of the mansion (and climactic shootout) from Scarface.

> Between the Malibu Club, the Pole Position, the shopping malls and the Pizza Stack restaurants - not to mention the various hotels, apartments and places of business that you acquire as you progress through the main story - this aptly named metropolis of iniquity is packed with places to go, NPCs to meet, and small but immersion-enhancing interactions.

> When you reminisce about Vice City today, alongside all the ultraviolence and automotive pyrotechnics, you're also likely to fondly recall the first time you went inside the Malibu Club, or the party mission aboard Colonel Cortez's yacht, or cruising down Ocean Beach in a convertible Stinger while listening to Broken Wings.

> In GTA: Vice City , released a mere 13 months after GTA 3, you are not constrained to the Dodo.

> Expanding on the comparatively austere GTA 3, in Vice City you can ride motorbikes, buy property, change your clothes, and discover unmarked ambient side missions such as robbing a pharmacy or beating up gang members to earn the 'good citizen' cash bonus.

> Nevertheless, two and a half decades on, some of the changes and enhancements made between GTA 3 and Vice City might sound superficial, or even faintly ridiculous.

> Vice City emerged in an era when the conventions of the 3D open-world game - especially the 3D open-world crime game - were still far from codified, when the mechanical language of the subgenre was unfinished.

> Or you could even go back to Grand Theft Auto, from 1997; the tasks that you receive in the top-down original version of Liberty City almost always involve driving somewhere, killing a bunch of people, picking something up and driving back, and that's also what you do for most of your time in Vice City.

> However, the magic of Vice City - and of videogames in general - lies in more than mechanics, mission design or any other tangibles of the form.

> Even though Vice City may have fundamentally the same structure and systems as GTA 3, True Crime, Mafia and many comparable crime capers that emerged during the '00s, it nevertheless feels like the standout because of its aesthetic approach.

> Prior to Vice City, the sensory thrills of GTA had been rooted largely in depravity, the transgressive excitement that comes from simulating actions and behaviours that are too dark, immoral and illegal for you ever to consider in reality.

> They're by no means fully grown up, but in Vice City, Rockstar's virtual fantasies appear more mature.

> With GTA 3, Rockstar succeeded in creating a 3D open playground; with Vice City, it started to develop and more finely shape what would eventually become its trademark - a rounded, reactive, and much more enveloping open world.

> Vice City's landscape is more than a racing track, and you're invited to regard its citizenry as more than digital toys for you to smash up in variously creative ways.

> But in Vice City - for the most part, at least - you have a reasonable understanding of why your character is doing the things he's doing.

> The effect is incomplete, and naturally primitive compared to much later games such as Cyberpunk 2077 , but in Vice City you can see that Rockstar is trying to unify the free-flowing, player-driven open world with cogent, coherent storytelling.

> Twenty-four years ago, Vice City's appeal might have laid in its new vehicles, its encompassing '80s soundtrack and its enormous cast of celebrity voices.

## GamesRadar+, 29 October 2026

[GTA 6 "felt too fast" when Rockstar made it run like Grand Theft Auto 5 due to the leap in visual performance over the past 13 years](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/grand-theft-auto/gta-6-felt-too-fast-when-rockstar-made-it-run-like-grand-theft-auto-5-due-to-the-leap-in-visual-performance-over-the-past-13-years/)

The outlet's own summary:

> I doubt Rockstar narrowing Vice City's roads to make them "more believable" helped either

> "If you want a pedestrian population to behave believably, and you can stand in front of them and produce an automatic shotgun out of nowhere and they don't react, then that doesn't work.

> With most of Rockstar still working on Red Dead Redemption 2 , the initial work on the project involved a small group traveling to Miami to get a better feel of what a return to Vice City would entail.

> While the roads of Los Santos are intentionally wider to make driving and turning easier, the roads of Vice City are narrower, as Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson wanted "a more believable size." The duration of day and night is also longer, giving you a greater window to get up to mischief under cover of night, if you so please.

> For example, Rockstar tested GTA 6 using GTA 5's timings and found that "everything felt too fast" for a world that boasts the level of fidelity that Vice City can reach.

> The citizens who call Vice City home were equally problematic.

> "As long as Valve is independent," analyst says it looks impossible Action RPGs Phantom Blade Zero is the 20-year culmination of a $7 indie RPG Crime Shows Michael C.

## Kotaku, 29 October 2026

[GTA 6 Is So Detailed, Rockstar Had To Make Its World Slower Than GTA 5's To Accommodate It - Kotaku](https://kotaku.com/gta6-is-so-detailed-rockstar-had-to-make-its-world-slower-than-gta5-to-accommodate-it-2000750634)

The outlet's own summary:

> Rockstar needed to make sunsets longer and let nighttime linger in order to make Vice City feel real

> If you want a pedestrian population to behave believably, and you can stand in front of them and produce an automatic shotgun out of nowhere and they don’t react, then that doesn’t work.

> If you want to summon a car in GTA 6 , you can pay a modest fee to use the Scooter Bros app.

> With the game’s visuals now more true-to-life, the company says it felt compelled to slow things down in order to maintain the immersion of Vice City.

> After rebuilding Vice City based on these excursions and the subsequent research, the company tested the world with the same time-and-day systems and gameplay speed as GTA5 , but something felt off. “Everything felt too fast,” Nelson explained. “As the resolution of the worlds goes up, I think there are things you can’t get away with in the same way.

## Push Square, 29 October 2026

[GTA-Inspired PS5 Open World Goes Full Tycoon in Upcoming Update](https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2026/10/gta-inspired-ps5-open-world-goes-full-tycoon-in-upcoming-update)

The outlet's own summary:

> Manage city logistics in new mode

> 8 Review Phantom Blade Zero (PS5) - One of the Generation's Greatest Action Exper...

Every report above is on the site's fixed source list. A report is not a confirmation: the mark on each linked entry says who said it.
